rendered_blocks.content: Your symptoms suggest postural imbalances affecting shoulder mechanics, thoracic alignment, and lower-body movement efficiency. The pectoral/trapecial pain during arm movement may stem from restricted ribcage expansion and compensatory muscle overuse. Hip rotation limitations and knee clicking likely relate to pelvic alignment, while foot pain could reflect gait compensation from these issues.

items: This exercise aims to improve rib cage mobility, enhance diaphragm function, and correct rounded shoulders by promoting full rib cage expansion and a stacked postural alignment. It involves a specific hand position, a gentle push through the ground, and a controlled exhale to engage core muscles, followed by a relaxed nasal inhale to expand the upper chest and back.

The primary cause of chronically tight upper traps and elevated shoulders is often a lack of proper circumferential ribcage expansion during inhalation, particularly in the posterior ribcage. When the body cannot expand the back of the ribcage sufficiently, it compensates by excessively sending air to the front of the ribcage and using accessory breathing muscles like the upper traps and neck to elevate the ribcage, leading to their tightness and elevation.
